learning_outcomes.text: Learns about the formation of fuels and the basic combustion properties of fuels.
Learns the theoretical information and reaction equations of combustion chemistry.
Have detailed information about combustion systems.
Learns the stoichiometric and emission calculations required for the combustion of fuels and becomes able to calculate them with at least one package program.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Fuels, combustion and combustion systems in engineering, combustion types, applications in economic sectors, business, energy and environment
Fossil fuels: Formation of coal, oil and natural gas, their production and processing. Classification of fuels, their properties and sectoral preference.

Fuel technologies: Production of technical fuels from rough solid, liquid and gaseous fuels. Fuel analyses, their interpretation from the design, operation and environmental effects points of view, conversion calculations of fuel analysis.
Definition and types of combustion, fundamental requirements of sustainable combustion. Fundamental mechanisms of combustion
Conversion mechanisms of fuel into gaseous form, fuel-air mixing, ignition and sustainable flame formation. Related design and operational measures.
Chemical thermodynamics, combustion reactions, chemical equilibrium and calculation of equilibrium constants, interpretations of equilibrium constants
Combustion analysis the solid-liquid and gaseous fuels, fuel consumption, combustion air and combustion products account. Emissivity of the flame and flue gases

Fuel preparation systems for coal, fuel oil and natural gas.
Experimental determination of combustion thermal performance and emission properties. Emission parameters and emission calculations
